raw_segments.text: That handkerchief did an Egyptian to my mother give.
She was a charmer and could almost read the thoughts of people.
She told her while she kept it, t'would make her amiable and subdue my father entirely
But if she lost it, or made a gift of it, my father's eye should hold her loathed,
and his spirits should hunt after new fancies.
She, dying, gave it me and bid me, when my fate would have me wive to give it her.
I did so, and take heed, aunt, make it a darling like your precious eye, to lose it or give
it away where such perdition as nothing else could match.
